title: Amazon's Jassy says AWS can win without the top AI model
excerpt: The AI race has been about who has the best model. That is changing, and Amazon is well placed to benefit.
content_html:
Amazon is proving you don't need the best model to win the AI race

By Eugene Kim

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Amazon's earnings on Thursday highlighted a surprising idea gaining traction across Silicon Valley: You don't need the best models to win in AI.

The company reported blockbuster results, including a 37% jump in revenue from Amazon Web Services. Those gains came from the cloud giant running many different AI models from leading providers such as Anthropic and OpenAI.

In contrast, Amazon's efforts to build its own models are in somewhat of a mess, as Business Insider reported earlier this week.

On Thursday, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy suggested this isn't a problem. During a call with analysts he said there won't be a single AI model that dominates the industry.

Instead, Jassy explained, customers increasingly want to use multiple leading models, a trend that's helped fuel the rapid growth of Amazon Bedrock, the company's platform for accessing foundation models.

"AWS and Amazon can have a wildly successful business without its own frontier model," Jassy said. "There is not going to be one model to rule the world."

This is a big change from what's been guiding much of the AI market since it exploded in 2022 on the back of ChatGPT. Companies have raced to develop the most powerful models, spending huge sums of money on training and other expensive development techniques.

Now, though, the race has evolved to be less about raw performance and more about building and running efficient models, so-called intelligence per dollar. This potentially suits Amazon more than some other AI rivals.

Amazon has never prioritized its own models. It did develop in-house offerings via the Nova range of models, but they struggled to come close to frontier.

More recently, the company has been overhauling its AI strategy, winding down most of the existing Nova line while shifting resources toward a new frontier-model initiative, Business Insider reported earlier this week.

Jassy's remarks suggest the company's long-term strategy is not to rely exclusively on its own models, but to make AWS the platform where customers can access the industry's leading AI systems — whether to not those come from Amazon.

Rather than trying to win solely on model performance, Amazon has focused on making Bedrock the centerpiece of it AI strategy. Last year, Jassy said AWS was "building Bedrock to be the biggest inference engine in the world" and predicted the service could eventually rival EC2, AWS's flagship cloud computing business.

During Thursday's call, Jassy said companies building AI applications want access to a wide range of models because different systems will surpass one another over time and excel at different tasks. That dynamic, he said, gives Bedrock a competitive advantage.

"If you're a company that's building important AI applications, you want to make sure that you have the ability to use all the available models," Jassy said. "They're going to each leapfrog each other at different times."

At the same time, Jassy made clear Amazon remains committed to developing its own AI models.

He said having a leading model would give the company greater control over costs for both its own consumer applications and AWS customers, while allowing Amazon to prioritize features important to customers and move faster without relying on outside providers.

Alexa, for example, has been reducing its reliance on Anthropic's costly models in favor of Amazon's own AI models to lower costs, Business Insider previously reported.

Jassy predicted that within the next few years there will be "at least a half dozen models that are comparably good to each other."

"They'll all be on Bedrock," he said, "and one of them will be ours."

content_html_zh:
亚马逊正在证明你不需要最好的模型来赢得人工智能竞赛

作者：Eugene Kim 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

亚马逊周四的财报突显了一个令人惊讶的想法，该想法在整个硅谷受到关注：你不需要最好的模型来赢得人工智能领域的胜利。

该公司公布了惊人的业绩，其中 Amazon Web Services 的收入增长了 37%。 这些收益来自于这家云巨头运行着来自 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 等领先提供商的许多不同的人工智能模型。

相比之下，正如《商业内幕》本周早些时候报道的那样，亚马逊建立自己的模式的努力有些混乱。

周四，亚马逊首席执行官安迪·贾西表示这不是问题。 在与分析师的电话会议中，他表示不会有单一的人工智能模型主导该行业。

Jassy 解释说，相反，客户越来越希望使用多种领先模型，这一趋势有助于推动 Amazon Bedrock（该公司用于访问基础模型的平台）的快速增长。

“即使没有自己的前沿模式，AWS 和亚马逊也可以拥有非常成功的业务，”贾西说。 “不会有一种模式来统治世界。”

自 2022 年 ChatGPT 推动人工智能市场爆发以来，这与引导大部分人工智能市场的方式相比是一个巨大的变化。 公司竞相开发最强大的模型，在培训和其他昂贵的开发技术上花费大量资金。

但现在，竞争已经不再是原始性能，而是更多地围绕构建和运行高效模型，即所谓的“每美元的智能”。 与其他一些人工智能竞争对手相比，这可能更适合亚马逊。

亚马逊从来没有优先考虑自己的模式。 它确实通过 Nova 系列模型开发了内部产品，但它们很难接近前沿。

据《商业内幕》本周早些时候报道，最近，该公司一直在彻底改革其人工智能战略，缩减现有 Nova 产品线的大部分，同时将资源转向新的前沿模型计划。

Jassy 的言论表明，该公司的长期战略不是完全依赖自己的模型，而是让 AWS 成为客户可以访问行业领先的人工智能系统的平台——无论这些系统是否来自亚马逊。

亚马逊并没有试图仅仅依靠模型性能取胜，而是专注于使 Bedrock 成为其人工智能战略的核心。 去年，Jassy 表示 AWS 正在“将 Bedrock 打造成世界上最大的推理引擎”，并预测该服务最终可能会与 AWS 的旗舰云计算业务 EC2 相媲美。

在周四的电话会议上，贾西表示，构建人工智能应用程序的公司希望获得广泛的模型，因为随着时间的推移，不同的系统将相互超越，并在不同的任务上表现出色。 他说，这种动态给 Bedrock 带来了竞争优势。

“如果你是一家正在构建重要人工智能应用程序的公司，你希望确保你有能力使用所有可用的模型，”贾西说。 “他们将在不同的时间超越对方。”

与此同时，贾西明确表示亚马逊仍然致力于开发自己的人工智能模型。

他表示，拥有领先的模型将使公司能够更好地控制自己的消费者应用程序和 AWS 客户的成本，同时允许亚马逊优先考虑对客户重要的功能，并在不依赖外部提供商的情况下更快地采取行动。

例如，据 Business Insider 此前报道，Alexa 一直在减少对 Anthropic 昂贵模型的依赖，转而使用亚马逊自己的人工智能模型来降低成本。

贾西预测，在未来几年内，将出现“至少六种彼此性能相当的型号”。

“它们都会在基岩上，”他说，“其中之一将是我们的。”
